You will own the functional strategy for your product area and coordinate with stakeholders across disciplines and levels to ensure the team is delivering high quality work which responds pragmatically to customer needs.

Alongside developing high quality product experiences, you will help evolve the design practice at Personio. Technical advances are enabling new tools and methods in the design process, and Personio is committed to exploring and integrating the latest possibilities.

This role is ideal for a candidate who is passionate about leveraging the latest technology and working with cross functional partners to solve customer needs.

  • Develop thoughtful and inclusive design strategies. Balance ambitious, insight-driven goals with practical constraints

  • Work at the leading edge of AI enabled workflows and bring new approaches to the design process

  • Create high fidelity deliverables (including hand-coded or AI-assisted prototypes) that articulate and inform product vision

  • Identify emerging design patterns and create reusable and extensible abstractions and frameworks, connecting disparate projects to avoid or reconcile avoidable divergence

  • Demonstrated commitment to uplifting the design through culture of excellence and empathetic support, mentoring designers and cross-functional peers and providing constructive critique and feedback

Role Requirements: What you need to succeed

  • Experience and passion for one or more dimensions of design, e.g., Product thinking, Interaction Design and Crafted execution

  • Skilled in using high-fidelity and AI powered prototyping tools

  • Experience in extending or creating reusable frameworks, tooling, rituals, playbooks, patterns or processes adopted by others that improve how teams work

  • Demonstrated ability to lead a product area in partnership with the cross functional team

  • Capable of elevating craft, proactively identifying and driving initiatives and raising quality across the product area

  • Proven track record of shipping high‑impact, multi-release product outcomes

  • Operates with autonomy, accountability, and mature decision-making thriving in ambiguity and can bring clarity to complex or undefined spaces

  • AI Fluency: You have hands-on experience using AI to improve your workflow, and the sound judgment to know exactly when to rely on it and when to step in yourself.

jobs.title: Product Owner WIFI, RF & Embedded Systems
jobs.description:
Chez Exotec, nous mettons l’excellence technologique au service de la redéfinition des relations entre humains et robots. A travers le monde, nos solutions révolutionnent la façon dont nos client·e·s délivrent leurs produits aux personnes consommatrices finales. Nous contribuons au succès des plus grandes marques du commerce et de l’industrie, tout en améliorant les conditions de travail de leurs salarié·e·s.

Par l’alliance de l’intelligence artificielle et d’un hardware performant, nos robots sont désormais déployés dans le monde entier et leur succès a fait de nous la première licorne industrielle française.

Rejoindre Exotec, c’est l’opportunité de donner du sens à vos compétences. Grandissez avec nos ExoPeople dans le monde entier pour faire de vos idées, des réalités.

La révolution robotique portée par Exotec ne fait que commencer, vous en êtes ?

Au sein de l'équipe Product Management ASRS, le Product Owner Connectivity est responsable de la stratégie produit, du développement, de la performance et de la fiabilité des solutions de connectivité déployées sur une flotte mondiale de plus de 12 000 robots autonomes.

Le Product Owner Connectivity pilote l'ensemble des solutions de communication sans fil utilisées au sein des systèmes robotiques et équipements associés. Il garantit leur performance, leur robustesse, leur évolutivité et leur conformité aux exigences opérationnelles et de sécurité.

Missions :

Solutions de connectivité

  • Pilotage des organes de sécurité utilisant des technologies RF.

  • Assurer la cohérence des solutions développées avec la stratégie technologique globale.

Profil

  • 8 à 10 ans d'expérience dans le développement de produits ou systèmes technologiques complexes, idéalement dans un environnement industriel.
  • Solides connaissances en connectivité sans fil (WiFi 5 GHz / 6 GHz, technologies RF, couverture, roaming et performance réseau).
  • Bonne compréhension des systèmes embarqués, de leurs architectures logicielles et des contraintes associées (temps réel, cybersécurité, sécurité fonctionnelle).
  • Connaissance des architectures électriques et systèmes industriels, avec la capacité à collaborer efficacement avec des experts hardware, software et systèmes.
  • Expérience du pilotage de sujets techniques complexes et de la coordination d'équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Excellentes capacités d'analyse, de résolution de problèmes, de communication et d'influence.
  • Fort intérêt pour l'innovation technologique, l'amélioration continue et les environnements industriels exigeants.

Benefits

  • Couverture mutuelle et prévoyance santé compétitive
  • Politique famille avantageuse
  • Programme de mobilité interne et internationale
  • Nombreuses opportunités de formation et de développement

Chez Exotec, nous garantissons l’égalité des chances dans notre processus de recrutement. L’ensemble des candidatures reçues sont étudiées indépendamment de l’âge, du genre, de l’origine, de la religion, de la couleur de peau, de la nationalité, du sexe, du handicap, de l’orientation sexuelle ou de toute autre distinction protégée par la loi.

Nous mettons en place un environnement de travail inclusif et respectueux de toutes les différences.
En rejoignant le Pacte Parité, Exotec s’engage pour un écosystème French Tech plus paritaire.

jobs.description:
The Fishbrain Team has built and maintains the #1 fishing app in the US, designed for people who are passionate about fishing and outdoors. Our mission is to deliver an incredible experience that helps anglers achieve their fishing dreams, today and tomorrow.

Want to take the #1 fishing app in the US with millions of users to the next level? Now's your chance! We're currently recruiting a Senior Product Designer to join our team at Fishbrain.

Why this role, why now

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Conversion team. You'll shape how millions of anglers discover Fishbrain, get started, and decide to go Pro.

Our conversion journey runs from the first search result to the first paid month. Right now, AI is reshaping what Fishbrain Pro can do, and we need a designer who can make that value obvious at every step. Your work shows up directly in our business metrics, so you'll see the impact of every decision you make.

The role

You'll be the designer in the Conversion team, working day to day with your PM and engineers. You report to our Head of Design and are part of a design guild with three other designers. Together you'll set the standards and rituals that raise the bar across Fishbrain.

You own the end-to-end experience for Conversion:

  • Acquisition: web and SEO pages that turn searches into app downloads

  • Monetization: trials, paywalls, subscription flows, and ad experiences

This is a senior role. Beyond delivery, you'll shape the team's roadmap and experiment strategy alongside your PM and EM.

What you'll be working on

  • Own the funnel end to end. Design high-quality, intuitive experiences from website to onboarding, trial, and subscription.

  • Move the numbers. Find gaps and opportunities in reg-to-trial, trial-to-Pro, website downloads, AI-visibility score and early retention.

  • Run experiments that teach us something. Shape hypotheses with your PM and EM, design for A/B tests, and read the results.

  • Keep discovery continuous. Talk to anglers regularly, prototype fast, and blend qualitative insight with data.

  • Make Pro's value clear. Show what Pro and AI-powered features like Fishing Intelligence do for anglers, without dark patterns.

  • Balance ads with experience. Design ad inventory that earns revenue without hurting the experience.

  • Raise the craft. Contribute to our design system, critiques, and guild standards in Figma and beyond.

  • Work AI-first. Use AI tools from research synthesis to coded prototypes, and help the guild find better ways of working.

What we’re fishing for

  • 5+ years in product design, with a portfolio that shows conversion or growth work and its measurable impact.

  • AI as part of your daily workflow, from discovery and synthesis to prototyping in code.

  • Strong mobile craft on iOS and Android, with a deep understanding of Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines and Material Design..

  • Web design experience, ideally SEO or landing pages built to drive app downloads.

  • Hands-on experimentation: you design for A/B tests and are comfortable in analytics tools like Amplitude.

  • Subscription or freemium experience, and an understanding of how people decide to pay.

  • Expert Figma skills across design systems, prototyping and handoff, and curiosity about the tools that come next.

  • A clear communicator who can explain the why behind a design to any stakeholder.

  • A degree in design, HCI or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Bonus, but not required

  • Fishing experience, or an eagerness to learn



Where you’ll work

We operate in a hybrid work environment, with all team members expected to work from our Stockholm HQ, The Lighthouse, located at Hötorget, at least three days a week.

We’re a product-focused startup, and every individual is important. That means you get to contribute to the direction of the company and the impact we have on millions of anglers. jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.description:
We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans.



But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.



To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest.



We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you.




LONDON (HYBRID, 3 DAYS IN OFFICE)

We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this position.



Marshmallow makes insurance work for everyone, including people the industry has overlooked. Your difference makes the difference, and we design for it.

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join our Telematics team. Telematics is a key part of Marshmallow’s future that sits within Acquisition and how we grow our user base. This is a mid-level role, ideally suited to someone with around 2–5 years of product design experience. You’ll have experience designing and shipping digital products, and you’re ready to take more ownership of your work while continuing to develop your craft.

In a nutshell, you’ll help more people get onboarded into Marshmallow by reducing friction in our sign up and activation flow. Longer term, you’ll be part of the team that build customer stickiness by working out how to reward and engage customers for being good drivers. You’ll work with a team that will back you up, and you’ll own problems from day one.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Starting with the problem. You’ll shape what we’re solving by doing research with customers, spotting patterns, and turning what you hear into clear themes and needs the team can act on.

 - Designing the whole journey. Wireframes, prototypes, flow to polished screens. You’ll be translating complex concepts into clear, benefit-led experiences. You’ll be thinking about the content on the screen and edge cases too. It’s primarily customer facing, web and app but if your work touches our internal tools, you’ll be thinking about that too.

 - Letting data point the way. You’ll use funnel and analytics data to find where customers get stuck and where we could be causing harm. Then you’ll work with your team to fix it.

 - Building with engineers. You’ll work alongside them from the first idea to what’s shipped. Clear specs and smooth handoffs. If a design tweak is quicker to ship yourself, you can raise the PR.

 - Working in a cross-functional team. Product managers, engineers, operations, data and other designers. You’ll continuously challenge and learn from each other.

 - Bringing stakeholders with you. Acquisition gets a lot of attention here. You’ll form your own opinions, explain your thinking, and keep people in the loop. You won’t be doing it alone, and we’ll help you build the skill.

 - Looking after the design system. Contribute to it, keep things consistent with our brand, and flag anything that doesn’t fit so we can sort it.

 - Using AI every day. For research, analysis and production. Try tools, keep what works, and share it with the team.


YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You have a commercial instinct. You have good gut instinct on what makes a product work and a portfolio that backs up what you’ve shipped having good business impact.

 - You have a proactive mind-set. You look to make continuous improvement to the products that you are working on. You find issues and features, write up tickets and ship them when they’re ready.

 - You are actively using AI. You’ve used AI to optimise your workflow and create efficiency gains whether that’s building prototypes,  shipping to production, analysing data or conducting research.

 - You prefer to ship quickly and learn. We like to move quickly and learn from real data. This means being able to spot when good is good enough and iterating.

 - You have 2+ years experience working somewhere fast moving (startup, fintech, scale-up etc).




PERKS OF THE JOB

 - Bonus scheme designed to reward high performance

 - Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva

 - Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year

 - Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose

 - 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

 - 4 weeks Work From Anywhere per year


OUR PROCESS

 - Initial call with a member from our Talent Team (30 mins)

 - Past Experience interview with Hiring Manager (60 mins)

 - Onsite Case Study session with a couple of the team (90 mins)

 - Culture interview (60 mins)

Diversity of thought

We know the best ideas come from having different perspectives in the room - and we're committed to hiring fairly, regardless of background, identity or experience. If you see yourself in this role, we'd encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer (m/f/d)
Lead Product Designer (100% Remote within Poland)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Docplanner's mission is to help people live longer, healthier lives. Every month about 100 million people visit our sites and 25 million appointments are booked across 13 countries, and 300,000 doctors use our software (docplanner.com http://docplanner.com).

You'll join PMS Global, the group building the software clinics and doctors run on. We're building Noa, our AI assistant, into the daily work of doctors and front desks. The group is organised in verticals named after the people they serve: the doctor running a visit, the owner running the business, the practice signing up on its own.

The design team here is small and growing. As its Lead designer, you'll set the standard others work to and help the team grow.


THE ROLE

You'll own the design of an area of our practice management software (PMS), the tools clinics use every day to run visits, calendars and the business. You'll set design direction across the teams in that area and shape how it fits with the rest of the product. You'll help decide whether something is worth building, and why, before anyone decides how. This is an individual contributor role.

We want clinics to spend less time on manual work, from documenting a visit to getting it invoiced and paid, and owners to see what needs their attention without digging through reports.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - After 3 months: you've been shipping since your first weeks, you can name the outcomes your area should move and the user behaviours behind them (where clinic staff lose time, work around the product or drop off), and you and product agree on the bigger problems worth solving. Clinics already feel it: your first fixes save front desks and doctors time on everyday tasks.

 - After 6 months: your first larger build is live with its impact measured, you're setting design direction across teams, and other designers are building on your patterns. For clinics this means less manual admin and fewer workarounds; for doctors, more time with patients and less time on the screen; for owners, a clearer view of how the practice is doing.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Discover continuously: talk to doctors, clinic owners and staff often, whatever project you're on.

 - Identify and solve bottlenecks: with product and engineering, find the friction points in the user journey and in how the team works, and fix them.

 - Drive clarity from complexity: balance user and business needs in areas like billing, records and reporting, and turn ambiguous problems into clear, strategic solutions.

 - Start with an LLM: use AI to clarify intent, draft short specs and surface risks and edge cases before opening a design tool.

 - Co-create with PMs and engineers from day one: define UX requirements early, stay through QA and release, and make engineering-aware decisions.

 - Shape high-leverage experiences: exceptional UI and UX for information-dense screens, from concept to polish, using the best tools to explore more directions faster and raise quality.

 - Prototype and build with AI: use Cursor and Claude Code to turn concepts into interactive prototypes and production-ready front-end code; move fluidly between code and Figma.

 - Validate and measure: run quick tests and track funnels, adoption and retention.

 - Lead without managing: set direction across teams, coach designers, and turn what works into patterns and practices others reuse.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Multi-disciplinary craft: strong UI, UX and visual design skills, with a track record of functional yet delightful experiences in information-dense, data-heavy products, ideally B2B SaaS. You write clear interface copy and can tell the story behind a design.

 - Comfortable in code: you prototype in code with AI tools and know enough HTML and CSS to work with engineers on the front end. You don't need to be a front-end engineer.

 - Experimentation mindset: a deep understanding of product metrics, behaviour analytics and A/B testing, and experience with Amplitude, Mixpanel or similar tools. Your portfolio shows experiments and measurable outcomes.

 - Passion and drive: deep care for product design and UX craft, and for the business outcomes they move. Ambition, ownership and a rising bar.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity: you work at speed without dropping quality, and know when to go deep and when to execute.

 - Reasoning: first-principles thinking, sharp structure, resistance to bias, attention to the details that matter.

 - Team spirit: generous, backs the best idea, hands-on, reliable, honest and transparent.

 - Lead-level scope: you've shaped direction across several teams or products, and other designers have grown by working with you.

 - Proficient English.


DESIGN AND AI AT DOCPLANNER

AI is changing how products are designed and built. We want our designers to explore how AI can improve both the design process and the product, from faster prototyping to Noa, the assistant inside our clinic software. We're looking for designers who are curious about new technology and experiment with AI in their own work. If you've worked on AI features or use AI tools in your design process, show us examples in your portfolio.

Let’s talk money

 - A salary adequate to your experience and skills.

True flexibility and work-life balance

 - Remote or hybrid work model with or hub in Warsaw;

 - Flexible working hours (fully flexible, as in most cases you only have to be on a couple of meetings weekly);

 - 20/26 days of paid time off (depending on your contract);

 - Additional paid day off on your birthday or work anniversary (you choose what you want to celebrate).

Health comes first

 - Private healthcare plan with Signal Iduna  https://www.signaliduna.pl/for you and subsidized for your family.

 - Multisport card co-financing for you to have access to sports facilities across Poland.

 - Access to iFeel https://ifeelonline.com/, a technological platform for mental wellness offering online psychological support and counseling.

Keep growing with us

 - Free English and Spanish classes.

When you apply for our roles you receive equal treatment regardless of age, disabilities, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or parental status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation or any other dimension of human difference. If you require additional support in your recruitment process, we kindly encourage you to let us know. Behind those words you’re reading, there’s a person (hi!) who already helped a candidate by adapting the interviews, and now we’re lucky to have this person with us. So, even if you’ve never asked for it before, may this serve as a sign that, now, you can do so. We can only truly be equal if we adapt to each other.

Reporting up through our Chief Product Officer, you'll work autonomously within your team while remaining connected to a centralized design group that is deeply collaborative and curious. If you want to do complex, meaningful work at the place where design and healthcare intersect, we'd love to hear from you!

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

Gusto’s looking to bring on several Staff Product Designers across our Money and HR Experience product organizations. These teams sit on some of the highest-stakes, most AI-native surfaces at Gusto, where small businesses make financial and people decisions that carry real impact, and where getting the experience right is what builds durable trust. That's exactly why judgment, taste, and craft matter here.

As a Staff Product Designer, you'll own experiences end to end within a specific domain, turning ambiguity into clear, trustworthy products and helping define patterns that don't yet exist at Gusto. You'll be deeply embedded in the product quartet, driving design decisions in partnership with Product Managers and Engineers, and demonstrating high craft and storytelling every step of the way.

This is one job posting for five open roles in Gusto Money, Banking, and HR Experiences product orgs. You'll be matched to the opportunity that best fits your strengths and interests. Here are the teams currently hiring:

  • Consumer Banking: Consumer Banking builds financial products for the millions of employees paid through Gusto, anchored to Gusto Wallet — spend accounts, savings goals, paycheck splitting, and on-demand access to earned wages. Because Gusto runs payroll, the team sits at the source of income itself, helping workers smooth cash flow between paychecks, save automatically, and avoid predatory alternatives like payday lenders and overdraft fees. One of the fastest-growing engines in Gusto Banking, it moves at a startup pace while incubating 0→1 foundational technology in a regulated space where trust, reliability, and craft are everything.

  • Gusto Money: MoneyOS is the team within Gusto Money focused on helping small businesses better understand, manage, and improve their financial position. This is an especially exciting moment for the team. The space is still taking shape, which means there’s real room to define the product, the patterns, and the customer expectations. MoneyOS works at the intersection of product strategy, financial systems, customer trust, and emerging AI-native ways of building—making it a strong fit for a designer who wants to have outsized influence on both what we build and how we build it.

  • HR Experiences (HRX): HRX helps small businesses get expert HR help right inside the product — a customer simply says what they need, and Gusto takes the action, answers the question, or brings in a human expert when the stakes are high. You'll design AI-native experiences across a two-sided service — the everyday self-serve moments, the AI that guides and does the work, and the human HR experts who step in when it matters most — so it all feels like one Gusto, in a domain where judgment and trust matter enormously.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day:

  • Own design end to end in your domain — from framing ambiguous problems to shipping high-craft, accessible experiences that hide the underlying complexity from customers.
  • Shape goals, priorities, and roadmap in partnership with your PM and engineering lead, balancing customer trust, business value, and technical realities.
  • Translate ambiguous, often 0→1 strategy into clear scopes, flows, and interaction patterns — including patterns that don't yet exist at Gusto.
  • Design the experience of AI thoughtfully — representing uncertainty, surfacing errors gracefully, preserving customer agency, and knowing when a human should step in.
  • Ground your decisions in customer insight, leading or partnering on research, competitive audits, and hypothesis-driven exploration in high-stakes, sometimes compliance-sensitive domains.
  • Raise the craft and systems bar, evolving Gusto's design system where existing patterns fall short.
  • Work in fast cycles and use AI tools in your own practice — set a clear target, prototype and ship real things to customers, and let what you learn sharpen the direction.

Here's what we're looking for:

  • 6+ years of product design experience owning and shipping end-to-end work, ideally in B2B SaaS, fintech, or another high-trust domain, with strong craft across web.
  • Experience designing AI-enabled or conversational experiences shipped to real users, and you can speak concretely to how you handled uncertainty, errors, and human override.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and 0→1, you frame the problem, scope the work, and move forward without waiting for perfect information.
  • Strong systems thinking, you use and contribute to a design system and know when to evolve it.
  • Judgment to evaluate and direct AI outputs, when to use them, when to override them, and how to raise the bar, especially where the cost of being wrong is high.
  • Strong collaboration and communication across design, product, engineering, and data.

Bonus points

  • Experience in a high-stakes or regulated domain, fintech, financial services, HR, compliance, legal, or healthcare.
  • Hands-on experience designing AI-driven or agentic product experiences, shaping how an AI or agent behaves, communicates, and hands off to a human.
  • Service-design fluency across two-sided or multi-stakeholder products: real journey mapping and blueprinting with operational handoffs, not workshop exercises.
  • Helped lead a team's shift to AI-native workflows, and can speak to what changed about the work itself, not just the tools.
  • Background contributing to AI governance, evaluation practices, or AI experience design patterns.

Our cash compensation range for this role is $146,000/yr to $183,000/yr in Denver, and $177,000/yr to $222,000/yr in San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. 

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer.

Headquarters: US - Remote

Elation Health exists to enable every patient to experience the highest quality care wherever they go in the healthcare system. We build technology for independent primary care practices and the physicians, clinicians, and teams who care for their patients every day.

Our platform brings together a clinical-first EHR, intelligent automation, billing, patient engagement, and the workflows that help primary care practices deliver excellent care and build sustainable businesses. The work is consequential: when our products are clear, trustworthy, and well designed, clinicians can spend more time focused on patients and less time fighting their tools.

Primary care is foundational to a healthy healthcare system, yet the technology supporting it is often fragmented, burdensome, and disconnected from the realities of clinical work. At Elation, Design has the opportunity to make the experience of practicing medicine meaningfully better—while helping independent primary care remain strong, sustainable, and human. 

We are seeking a passionate Design leader to drive our design strategy, build a strongly capable Design organization, raise the quality and coherence of the product experience, and use AI-native ways of working to deliver more intuitive, trusted, and impactful experiences for clinicians and practices at scale. If you’re excited about shaping the next generation of AI-native primary care technology, this role is for you.

The opportunity

As Head of Design, you will set the vision, standards, and operating model for Design at Elation. You will lead a talented team of product designers and design partners, work closely with Product and Engineering leadership, and bring a strong design point of view to company strategy and product decisions.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between the strategic and the concrete: defining a coherent experience across a complex product, coaching designers through difficult problems, raising the quality bar, and ensuring the details hold up in the hands of real clinicians.

You will report to the Chief Product Officer and serve as a senior voice in the Product Development organization. The title and scope will be calibrated to the experience and demonstrated impact of the person we hire.

What you’ll do

  • Set and communicate a clear design vision for Elation’s product experience, grounded in our clinical-first principles and the realities of primary care.
  • Lead and shape an AI-native Design organization with a durable operating model for how designers, agents, and cross-functional teams work together to create higher-quality experiences at greater speed. Elation is already well on this journey, with AI-native product strategy, evolving design systems, and emerging AI-assisted design-review practices.
  • Build a high-performing Design function: clarify roles and responsibilities, establish effective operating rhythms, create growth paths, and hire and retain exceptional design talent.
  • Partner with the CPO, product leaders, engineering leaders, and executive stakeholders to translate company strategy into a focused product experience strategy and roadmap.
  • Raise the quality bar across the end-to-end user experience, including research, service design, product strategy, interaction design, visual design, content, accessibility, and customer enablement.
  • Strengthen the systems that allow design to scale: principles, patterns, documentation, design systems, research practices, reusable frameworks, and the connection between design artifacts and shipped product. Implement a practical design-review culture that improves decisions early, creates shared standards, protects team velocity, and makes quality everyone’s responsibility.
  • Foster deep empathy for clinicians and practice teams by embedding a rigorous culture of user research across product development—engaging directly with clinical and billing experts through co-design, workflow observation, and qualitative and quantitative insights.
  • Help teams solve the right problems before they move quickly on the wrong ones. Create clarity in ambiguous spaces and make tradeoffs explicit.
  • Partner closely with Engineering to ensure that design intent survives implementation and that the finished experience is reliable, coherent, accessible, and delightful to use.
  • Develop designers as leaders and active contributors to product direction—not simply as owners of screens or deliverables.
  • Represent the customer and the design perspective in senior leadership discussions, product prioritization, launch decisions, and company-wide conversations about quality.
  • Create an environment where designers can do their best work: one that is candid, collaborative, intellectually curious, and accountable for impact.

We will measure success through a combination of customer impact, product quality, organizational health, and operating leverage. In particular, we expect this leader to improve:

  • The quality and consistency of customer insight used in product decisions.

jobs.title: Head of Design
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Germany (Remote); London, United Kingdom; Poland (Remote); Romania (Remote)

At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

 

About the role

We're looking for a Head of Design who still loves to design. You'll lead a small, strong team of product designers, set the bar for craft and for how we work with AI, and spend about half your time designing with some of our teams.

Ledgy's problems are dense and high-stakes: finance, legal and HR teams use us to manage real ownership and real money across many countries. Design here has to be precise and still feel simple. As the company grows into new markets and new products, you'll shape what design at Ledgy becomes.

Design at Ledgy is AI-first. Work starts with AI models, moves into working prototypes in our codebase, and lands in Figma for the system. Every team ships agent features. You'll make sure the whole team does this well, consistently, and with judgement.

Reports to: VP of Product

Location: Hybrid from our London office, remote in the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland or Romania

What you'll do

Lead the team (~50%)

  • Manage and grow three product designers working across our product teams: regular 1:1s, honest feedback, clear growth paths.
  • Hire: help shape roles, run interviews and grow the team as Ledgy grows.
  • Partner with product and engineering leadership on planning, staffing and the design vision across all teams.
  • Own the direction of our design system and shared AI patterns (how agents ask, act, explain and undo), together with engineering.
  • Define how we design with AI: tools, workflows, prototypes in code, shared skills and prompts. Make it easy for every designer to work this way.
  • Run design critique and design reviews, and own the quality bar across the product.

Design hands-on (~50%)

  • Be the designer for one of our teams (for example Tax, Trading, AI Systems - to be decided together): contribute to Ledgy’s product experiences, from agents and AI-assisted workflows to the our trading integrations and compliance reporting
  • Prototype in code in our real codebase, and open small front-end PRs when it's faster than a handoff.
  • Set the example: work in the open, show your thinking, ship.

You'll thrive here if you

  • Have 10+ years in product design on complex B2B or data-dense products, including 2+ years leading or managing designers.
  • Still design and prototype yourself, and want to keep doing it.
  • Are AI-native: you know when to prototype, when to stop and think, which tool fits which job, and how to turn that into habits a team can share.
  • Understand how AI agents work well enough to design for them and argue with engineers about them: the model, the harness, tool calls, APIs, audit trails.
  • Build your own tools: prompts, skills, small automations, and help others build theirs.
  • Raise quality through people, not just through your own work: you've grown designers and improved how a team works.
  • Communicate clearly with leadership and influence decisions across product and engineering. Fluent English.

Nice to have

  • Experience in equity, fintech, tax, payroll or accounting software.
  • Led design for AI or agent products that shipped to real customers.
  • Built or evolved a design system in code.

What your journey could look like

  • First 30 days: Meet every designer, PM and EM; learn the product and our customers; review how the team works today.
  • First 3 months: Run the team's rituals, ship your first work, and propose how design should work with AI across teams.
  • 6–12 months: Grow the team, raise the craft bar visibly, and set the design vision for the next stage of Ledgy.

Our interview process

  1. Recruiter call (30 min): you, us, the role, logistics.
  2. Hiring manager interview (45 min): how you work, lead and decide.
  3. Portfolio presentation (60 min): two projects, at least one showing how you work with AI, and one story about building or leading a team.
  4. AI working session (3.5h, live): frame a problem with a PM and a designer, build it with your own AI tools, and critique a piece of work as you would with your team.
  5. Final interview (45 min): with one of our founders.

You'll get a short guide before each step.
